examples.text: The wave traveled from the center of the lake before breaking on the shore.

The new sea wall may stop the waves from the sea, but not from the children who enthusiastically greet our train as it passes. It's great to see this ages-old habit is still going strong.

examples.text: He dismissed her with a wave of the hand.

glosses: A sudden, but temporary, uptick in something.

examples.text: A wave of shoppers stampeded through the door when the store opened for its Christmas discount special.
A wave of retirees began moving to the coastal area.
A wave of emotion overcame her when she thought about her son who was killed in battle.

examples.text: As the player eliminates each wave of 55 aliens, the next wave begins lower than the one previous.

To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.

examples.text: The flag waved in the gentle breeze.

glosses: To move one's hand back and forth (generally above the shoulders) in greeting or departure.

examples.text: I raised my arms in a final salute. I smiled. I waved goodbye. I turned into the helicopter, the door was closed, the red carpet was rolled up.

glosses: To call attention to, or give a direction or command to, by a waving motion, as of the hand; to signify by waving; to beckon; to signal; to indicate.

examples.text: I waved goodbye from across the room.
Look, with what courteous action / It waves you to a more removed ground.

glosses: To have an undulating or wavy form.

examples.text: horns whelked and waved like the enridged sea

glosses: To style (the hair) so as to produce a wavy texture.

examples.text: The starter waved the flag to begin the race.

examples.text: He waved indifferently 'twixt doing them neither good nor harm.
